scope_decision: All 30 pairs retained with their originally authored polarity; no author edits were required. This records the pre-observation semantic rubric, not an Engine outcome.
positive_rule: The separate direct target launch anchor is not denied. Each adverse role is completely bound either to a non-launch physical/printed property or one named foreign event; a foreign document owner alone is not an event owner.
negative_rule: Each negative contains explicit target launch/existence/global denial, an unresolved owner/referent, a mixed or conflicting event owner, or a real owner-bearing context gap. Both no requested_relation and non-Relevant are required by the unchanged inherited scorer.
raw_risk_rule: Raw scope risk is an independent axis. li22-024 and li22-048 have actual owner gaps and are semantic negatives for that reason, not for the raw enum alone. Pure raw-risk-only joint negatives:0. Exact raw/effective values will be saved without asserting hidden component preservation/loss from the resulting enum.
clarifications: Pair03 and pair11 distinguish ink/layout of a quoted event sentence from a present assertion withdrawing that event.
Pair12/13/14/15 permit an explicit same-role single foreign supplement only for an unowned launch role. Existing target owner, competing supplements, or a property-only owner remain negative.
Pair21/22 use complete role declarations in title/heading and explicit role references in excerpt; no arbitrary document graph is requested.
Pair23 explicitly declares Heron Clip as the full canonical name with no actual gap; its negative still directly withdraws the target event.
Pair24 treats missing-owner words inside a complete underline property as literal text; actual missing footer and event owner remain negative.
Pair27/28 require each reporting/time-linked clause to have a complete safe scope, without deriving chronology.
Pair29/30 keep document/property owner separate from the complete event owner.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: seal-property versus target launch denial
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The fully named Object concerns only a physical seal shape; its withdrawal does not negate launch.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The reason clause explicitly negates target launch in addition to withdrawing a physical property.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: foreign certificate property versus global notice denial
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: A complete physical property on the explicitly foreign product certificate is denied.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The whole notice and the target launch statement are explicitly retracted.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: literal non-event text as ink property versus assertion
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The Object is the ink color of a literal sentence in a named foreign insert, not the truth of that sentence.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: A separate present assertion directly denies the target event.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: spine-property correction versus target existence denial
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The withdrawn manual binding property and maintained cover property are explicitly non-launch.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The contrast clause independently denies the existence of the canonical target.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: printed units versus same-target event correction
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The Object refers to printed table units even though the booklet belongs to the target.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The explicit second denial concerns the target launch itself.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: caption alignment versus unresolved additional launch claim
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The caption alignment Subject is complete and non-launch.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: A separately withdrawn launch claim has no named owner and may cover the target anchor.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: paper texture and measured property versus target non-event
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: Both named roles describe complete physical paper properties of a foreign document.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The while clause adds an explicit target non-event that cannot be erased by safe property roles.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: heading text property versus broad launch withdrawal
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The literal heading containing Launch is a type-style property with a full foreign document owner.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The later withdrawal explicitly covers every launch statement and the target.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: foreign event plus foreign physical property versus unnamed event
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The event Object and physical Subject have an explicit unique foreign owner.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The full foreign owner belongs only to the physical property and cannot fill the ownerless event.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: foreign manual quote event versus target event quoted in foreign manual
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The withdrawn event explicitly belongs to Bracken Lens, independently of the manual owner.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: A foreign manual does not make its explicitly target-owned quoted event foreign.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: foreign document publication property versus target launch quoted content
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The full Object is a printed line-count property, despite target launch words inside the heading.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The full Object is expressly the target event; layout information is incidental.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: same-role immediate owner supplement versus actual owner gap
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: An otherwise unowned typed event receives one complete immediate same-role foreign owner.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The event has an actual missing owner; no foreign property elsewhere can authorize a loan.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: owner heading supplementation versus explicit target owner retained
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The explicit heading supplies a unique foreign owner to the otherwise unowned typed Object.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: A heading supplement cannot overwrite an already target-owned event declaration.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: reply owner supplement versus competing supplements
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The adjacent reply explicitly identifies the sole event owner as a complete foreign product.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: Two owner statements conflict and include the target; the event cannot be safely foreign.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: newline owner supplementation versus property-only owner
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: A single full foreign owner directly follows the same-role owner marker on the next line.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The only named owner is for a property Subject; the event Object remains expressly ownerless.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: foreign event apposition versus target event apposition
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The immediate complete claim apposition identifies a unique foreign event.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The immediate apposition identifies the target event despite a foreign stationery name.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: explicit property denial object versus broader quoted event
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The complete apposition is a physical engraving-depth property, not an event denial.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The apposition explicitly states the target launch claim and retracts that event.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: two property roles plus foreign event versus target event
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: All three roles are complete; the event is foreign and the other two are physical properties.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The middle role expressly owns the target event and remains adverse among safe property roles.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: two foreign events and document property versus ownerless third event
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The two withdrawn events name complete foreign owners and the third role is printed border color.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: Two foreign events cannot resolve the independently ownerless third launch role.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: property context before separate whole-source denial
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: Every adverse role concerns a complete physical or printed sleeve property.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: An independent source-title retraction explicitly invalidates the whole source and its target launch claim.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: typed property in title versus typed event in title
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The title fully declares a non-launch page-fold property; the excerpt refers to the same role.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The title fully declares a target-owned launch role that is denied in the excerpt.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: property heading versus unresolved claim in independent field
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The heading and role reference completely specify a non-launch lettering property.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The separate withdrawn launch claim is ownerless despite a fully owned property heading.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: complete canonical name versus actual target denial with clip note
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: A complete canonical Clip name has no actual gap and the adverse Item is a magnetic-clasp property.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The same complete-name note cannot neutralize an explicit target launch withdrawal.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: complete literal missing-owner print property versus real context gap
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: Literal uncertainty words are inside a complete printed property, with no missing event context.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The owner-bearing footer is genuinely missing; the denied event is not safely bound to a foreign owner.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: maintained foreign non-event plus safe property versus maintained target nonexistence
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The property role and the maintained non-event both have explicit foreign scope.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The maintained nonexistence of the target is independent of the safe foreign property role.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: parenthesized full property correction versus parenthesized target denial
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The parenthesized correction explicitly repeats the same complete physical property scope.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The parenthesis adds an independent explicit target non-event instead of a property explanation.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: reporting clauses with complete foreign ownership versus owner ambiguity
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The reporting clause names the same foreign event; the second role is a complete paper property.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The additional reported non-event and denied role have an expressly unknown product owner.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: time connector between safe corrections versus separate target denial
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: No chronology is inferred; the two adversely corrected clauses are a complete property and a foreign event.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The final and clause explicitly denies the target event regardless of the other two scopes.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: different role owners in one document versus mixed event ownership
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: Each role has an independently complete scope: a title punctuation property and a foreign launch.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The adverse event role explicitly mixes the target and a foreign owner and cannot be excluded as foreign.

pair_scope_reviews.axis: neutral document owner supplement versus explicit event owner
pair_scope_reviews.positive_basis: The adverse roles are a full printed property and a unique foreign event; publisher metadata is not event ownership.
pair_scope_reviews.negative_basis: The Item explicitly names the target event despite a foreign document owner and a safe property correction.

newness: All scenarios authored after source21 freeze using new combinations/content. The known iterative failure history informed boundaries; public schema and finite role grammar are intentionally shared. No old author/case/input or unused draft text was read or transformed for this authoring; statistical independence or cross-corpus improvement is not claimed.
